<margin>To be a person of refinement, to obtain a refined wife, to have refined friends, and to associate with a refined daughter, all written with a refined pen. Refined people, refined words, refined affairs, refined writing. I have not yet managed to read this in my life, nor have I seen such a book.</margin>

Oulongan was once robbed. He had stored a case of cups and bowls; the velvet lining remained as it was, yet the vessels were all gone. These were double-falsehoods, impossible to fathom. Liu laughed and said, "One by one, do not bother to investigate them further."

Jiaona

Scholar Kong, a descendant of the Sage <note>Referring to Confucius</note>, was a man of refinement who excelled at poetry. He had a close friend living in Tiantai who sent a letter to invite him. Kong traveled there, but it happened that he arrived just as his friend passed away. Being destitute and unable to return home, he resided in Putuo Temple, working for the monks as a copyist. About a hundred paces west of the temple was the residence of Master Dan. The Master was a descendant of a noble family who, due to a major lawsuit, had seen his family fortunes decline. With few dependents left, he moved to the countryside, leaving his town house vacant. One day, with snow falling heavily and the path silent and devoid of travelers, Kong happened to pass by the gate. A youth came out, possessed of a most distinguished bearing. Upon seeing Kong, he hastened to greet him and offered formal courtesies, inviting him to visit. Kong, feeling delighted, readily followed him in. The house was not very large, but everywhere were hung silk curtains, and the walls were covered with the paintings and calligraphy of the ancients. On the desk lay a book with a label that read: "Trifles from Langhuan" <note>A mythological library of the immortals.</note>.

<summary>This page introduces the story of Scholar Kong, a refined descendant of Confucius who, finding himself stranded after a failed visit to a friend, begins a fateful acquaintance with a distinguished youth in a vacant noble residence.</summary>
